blocks.text: Setting up your legal document environment in Pages

Efficiency in legal transcription starts with a clean document setup. You should avoid starting from scratch every time. Create custom templates in Pages that include your firm's specific margins, font requirements, and line numbering. Go to File > Save as Template to keep your formatting consistent across all client files.

Legal documents often require specific headers and footers for case numbers and document titles. Use the View > Show Layout menu to see your margins clearly. If you need to add page numbers, go to Insert > Page Number. Ensure your document is set to the correct paper size in the Document sidebar, usually US Letter for most jurisdictions.

Speed comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Use Command + B for bolding speaker names, Command + I for italics on legal citations, and Command + U for underlining headings. These shortcuts save seconds that add up over a full day of work.

items: Command + Shift + L: Show or hide layout boundaries to check spacing.
Command + R: Show or hide the ruler for precise margin adjustments.
Command + K: Quickly add a hyperlink to a legal reference or external file.
Control + Command + Space: Open the Character Viewer for special symbols like the section sign (§).

blocks.text: Transcripts often involve multiple speakers and long blocks of dialogue. Use the Styles sidebar to create specific paragraph styles for 'Speaker' and 'Dialogue'. This allows you to apply formatting to entire sections with one click. If you find yourself typing the same phrases repeatedly, use the macOS System Settings > Keyboard > Text Replacements feature to create shortcuts for common legal terms.

Lazur works as a voice assistant that sits in your Mac's notch. You can hold Option + Command to ask about any tool on your screen. If you forget where a specific formatting menu is, ask Lazur to point it out. It will circle the button or menu item for you. This is useful when you are deep in a long document and do not want to break your focus to search through menus.

One common error is failing to verify the document format after exporting from Pages to Word. Clients often require .docx files. Always perform a final check after saving to Word format. Look for broken tables or missing headers. Another mistake is relying solely on automated dictation for sensitive names or case numbers. Always proofread these sections manually.
Security and privacy for legal documents

Legal transcription requires high standards for data privacy. Pages allows you to password-protect your documents directly. Go to File > Set Password to encrypt your files. When using voice assistants like Lazur, ensure you understand that your audio is not stored or used for training models. This keeps your client data secure while you use modern tools to assist with your workload.

faq.question: Can I use Pages for official court transcripts?
faq.answer: Yes, provided you set up your document to meet the specific formatting requirements of your jurisdiction regarding margins, line numbering, and font styles.

faq.question: How do I ensure my Pages documents open correctly in Microsoft Word?
faq.answer: Export your document using File > Export To > Word. Always review the resulting file for layout shifts, especially regarding tables and complex headers.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle long audio files in Pages?
faq.answer: Pages is a word processor, not an audio player. Use a dedicated playback tool like Express Scribe alongside Pages, and use your voice or keyboard to input text as you listen.
